- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), then underestimates later (last 10–20 days).  
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), then correct downward — suggesting model fails to capture mean reversion after volatility peaks.  
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates a falling trend until 2–3 days later.  
- Forecast mean is typically 2–4% higher than true outcome, indicating a persistent upward bias.  
- Model struggles with short-term reversals (e.g., 1–2 day swings) — often fails to adjust forecast direction quickly.  
- In periods of high volatility, model overreacts to recent data, leading to overfitting to recent spikes.  
- Model underestimates the true long-term trend (e.g., 30-day average) — suggests it doesn’t adequately weight historical momentum.  
- Forecasts often peak too early — model anticipates a peak before the actual peak, then fails to adjust downward.  
- Model tends to ignore or underweight the influence of policy or supply-demand shocks in the immediate future.  
- In low-volatility periods, model underestimates the true price — suggesting it’s too conservative in the absence of strong signals.
